title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
claim: Timer-M1 is a pretrained multivariate model with target, past-only and known-future covariate roles that the authors report first on FEV and TIME and second on GIFT-Eval among recent foundation models.
why_relevant: A known-future-covariate model that could in principle take temperature; no wrapper in spec.yaml, and public weights were not confirmed in this scan.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
claim: Selecting the latest weather run issued before a GB auction gate picks a run not yet published at the gate on more than 99% of days for six of ten weather-model configurations, and the apparent accuracy effect of that leak ranges from -9% to +24%, so it must be measured rather than assumed.
why_relevant: A direct check on our no-lookahead rule for the forecast weather regime: issue time is not availability time; about market data and prices, not a load model.

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
claim: A preregistered 96-hour comparison in nine Nordic zones: three zero-shot models beat SARIMA and GBM baselines on the 2025 test, but the holdout difference was inconclusive.
why_relevant: Pre-registered multi-day hourly energy-series backtest of zero-shot models; carbon intensity rather than load.
